# Tools

The scripts in `tools/`. The text of each section is the docstring at the top of the script.

## `generate_fields_yaml.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/generate_fields_yaml.py)

```text
Generate defs/fields/nd10-fields.yaml, nd500-fields.yaml, nd5000-fields.yaml
from the C# field files ND10Fields.cs, ND500Fields.cs, ND5000Fields.cs.

Usage:
    python3 tools/generate_fields_yaml.py nd10   <ND10Fields.cs>   [out.yaml]
    python3 tools/generate_fields_yaml.py nd500  <ND500Fields.cs>  [out.yaml]
    python3 tools/generate_fields_yaml.py nd5000 <ND5000Fields.cs> [out.yaml]

The C# file is passed as an argument (no hard-coded path). Default output is
defs/fields/<model>-fields.yaml next to this tools/ folder.

nd500 and nd5000: `partition:` lists the non-overlapping fields, highest bit
first; `subfields:` lists the fields that overlap the partition.
nd10: `fields:` lists every named field; the fields overlap on purpose, and
`format:` says which of the four micro instruction formats the field is used
in (ARITHMETIC, INTERBLOCK, JUMP, LOOP, joined with |, or ALL).
```

## `generate_tokens_yaml.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/generate_tokens_yaml.py)

```text
Generate YAML token definitions from the existing ND110Compile C# source files.

This tool reads ND110Tokens.cs and ND120Tokens.cs and produces:
  - defs/tokens/nd110-tokens.yaml
  - defs/tokens/nd120-tokens.yaml

Tokens present only in ND-120 are marked with `nd120_only: true` in nd120-tokens.yaml.
Tokens whose encoding matches between ND-110 and ND-120 are marked as `models: [nd110, nd120]`.

The encoding is preserved as octal strings to match the original C# source.

Token category inference rules (derived from the token name prefix):
  A,*   -> A_REG
  B,*   -> B_REG
  AB,*  -> AB_REG
  PIC,* -> PIC
  ALUF,* -> ALUF
  ALUD,* -> ALUD
  ALUM,* -> ALUM
  STS,* -> STS
  CRY,* -> CRY
  MIS,* -> MIS
  IDBS,* -> IDBS
  COMM,* -> COMM
  T,*   -> T_SEQ or T_STK based on suffix
  F,*   -> F_SEQ or F_STK based on suffix
  COND,* -> COND
  LCOUNT/CONDENABL/XRF -> SPECIAL
```

## `generate_tokens_yaml_nd10.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/generate_tokens_yaml_nd10.py)

```text
Generate defs/tokens/nd10-tokens.yaml from the C# file ND10Tokens.cs.

Usage:
    python3 tools/generate_tokens_yaml_nd10.py <ND10Tokens.cs> [out.yaml]

The C# file is passed as an argument (no hard-coded path). Default output
is defs/tokens/nd10-tokens.yaml next to this tools/ folder.

Every call has the shape
    Add("NAME", <expression>, "comment");
where the expression uses Bit(n), At(low, value), the constants declared in
the file (OP_INTB, OP_JUMP, OP_LOOP, LOG, MOST, COND), | and plain numbers.
The two for-loops (LE0..LE17 and B,B0..B,B17) are expanded here.

parts is 2 octal strings, MSB part first: bits 31-16, bits 15-0.
Category comes from the section header comment ("// ---- Title ---") that
precedes the Add call.
```

## `generate_tokens_yaml_nd500.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/generate_tokens_yaml_nd500.py)

```text
Generate defs/tokens/nd500-tokens.yaml from the C# file ND500Tokens.cs.

Usage:
    python3 tools/generate_tokens_yaml_nd500.py <ND500Tokens.cs> <ND500Fields.cs> [out.yaml]

The C# files are passed as arguments (no hard-coded paths). Default output
is defs/tokens/nd500-tokens.yaml next to this tools/ folder.

Each AddToken call has the shape
    AddToken("NAME", f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8, f9, "comment");
with f1..f9 = control store parts CS8..CS0, octal strings, CS8 first.

Category rule: the partition field (ND500Fields.Partition) that holds all
bits of the token; ZERO when no bit is set; ARG when any bit is below
bit 32; MULTI when the bits lie in more than one partition field.
```

## `generate_tokens_yaml_nd5000.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/generate_tokens_yaml_nd5000.py)

```text
Generate defs/tokens/nd5000-tokens.yaml from the C# file ND5000Tokens.cs.

Usage:
    python3 tools/generate_tokens_yaml_nd5000.py <ND5000Tokens.cs> <ND5000Fields.cs> [out.yaml]

The C# files are passed as arguments (no hard-coded paths). Default output
is defs/tokens/nd5000-tokens.yaml next to this tools/ folder.

Two kinds of C# call:
    AddToken("NAME", "FIELD", value, "comment");   value << lowBit of FIELD
    AddMemToken("NAME", code, "comment");          code bit 3 -> bit 41,
                                                   code bits 2-0 -> bits 34-32

parts is 8 octal strings, MSB part first: bits 127-112 ... bits 15-0. The
part of bit n is 7 - n/16, as ND5000TokensBase.OrValueIntoWords does.
Category is the FIELD argument, or MEM for AddMemToken.
```

## `nd100-combine.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/nd100-combine.py)

```text
Combine/split ND-100 PROM images.

The ND-100 CPU uses many small 82S185 PROMs (2K x 8-bit, of which only
the low 4 bits are used) instead of the ND-110/120's two large EPROMs.
Each PROM provides 4 bits of the 48-bit microinstruction word at a
single slot position on the PCB.

Card variants in reference/roms/ND100/
--------------------------------------
3033S (base)   — 19 PROMs:
    d5..d16  (12 chips, 01504-01515 N rev)  = 48-bit microcode  data
    d17..d20 ( 4 chips, 01500-01503 P/Q)    = sequencer / next-address
    b18..b20 ( 3 chips, 01600-01602 N)      = instruction-decode PLA
                                              (addressed by macro opcode)

3033E-CX (extended)  35 PROMs:
    d5..d16  (12 chips, 01504-01515 N - d15=01705N replacement)
                                            = 48-bit microcode  data (base)
    d17..d20 ( 4 chips, 01500-01503 P/Q)    = sequencer (same as 3033S)
    c5..c16  (12 chips, 08504-08515 D/E)    = 48-bit microcode  (extension)
    c17..c20 ( 4 chips, 08500-08503 D)      = sequencer (extension)
    b18..b20 ( 3 chips, 08600-08602 D)      = decode PLA (CX version)

Every PROM is addressed by an 11-bit microaddress (0..2047) and returns
a 4-bit output. 12 PROMs in parallel form a 48-bit microword per
address. Combining the image is a simple interleave:

    for addr in 0..2047:
        word = 0
        for chip_index in 0..11:
            word |= chip[chip_index][addr] << (chip_index * 4)

Bit ordering convention
-----------------------
Physical bottom (d5 / c5) holds the LOW nibble (bits 0-3); physical top
(d16 / c16) holds the HIGH nibble (bits 44-47). This convention matches
the typical TTL schematic numbering where the lowest-numbered chip maps
to the lowest-weight bit.

Output
------
A `.CODE`-style file with 8 bytes per address (6 bytes of microcode,
little-endian, padded to 8 so it matches the ND-110/120 .CODE layout
used elsewhere in this repo). Preceded by a 2-byte little-endian
address. 10 bytes per record.

Addresses with "empty" (all-zero) microcode are NOT written, matching
the reference ND110Compile compiler output convention.
```

## `validate.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/validate.py)

```text
YAML Validator for ND-100/110/120 Microcode Definitions

Validates that the YAML token definitions in defs/tokens/ correctly describe
the actual microcode by:

  1. Loading the YAML definitions
  2. Loading a .CODE binary file
  3. Disassembling each word using the YAML token lookup
  4. Comparing against the corresponding .uc source file (if available)
  5. Reporting any discrepancies

Usage:
    python3 validate.py [--model nd110|nd120] [--binary path.CODE] [--source path.uc]

Default: validates ND-110 RASK against reference/ND-110-RASK.CODE
```

## `validate_new_models.py`

[Source](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/tools/validate_new_models.py)

```text
Check defs/tokens/nd10|nd500|nd5000-tokens.yaml and defs/fields/*-fields.yaml
against the C# files they were generated from.

Usage:
    python3 tools/validate_new_models.py <folder with the C# files>

The folder holds ND10Tokens.cs, ND10Fields.cs, ND500Tokens.cs, ND500Fields.cs,
ND5000Tokens.cs, ND5000Fields.cs. Nothing is written. Exit code 1 on any
difference in name, bits, count, category or description.

The C# files are read with the parsers of the three generator scripts in this
folder. On top of that the checks below do not use the generators' own output
path: they recompute every value from the C# data and compare it to what
PyYAML reads back from the YAML files.
```
